elements.title: NASA Engineer Cindy Fuentes Rosal waves goodbye to a Black Brant IX sounding rocket
elements.content:
A NASA engineer seen from behind, wearing a blue cap and a jacket labeled “ROCKET SCIENTIST,” waves toward a Black Brant IX sounding rocket launching into the sky from a field at NASA’s Wallops Flight Facility.

Caption: NASA Engineer Cindy Fuentes Rosal waves goodbye to a Black Brant IX sounding rocket launching from NASA’s Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia during the total solar eclipse on April 8, 2024. The rocket was part of a series of three launches for the Atmospheric Perturbations around Eclipse Path (APEP) mission to study the disturbances in the electrified region of Earth’s atmosphere known as the ionosphere created when the Moon eclipses the Sun. The rockets launched before, during, and after peak local eclipse time on the Eastern Shore of Virginia.

Photo credit: NASA/Chris Pirner
